title: Frontend stack for the customer portal
context: You are building a **customer portal**: logged-in users view invoices and open support tickets. The team has **two developers**, both strong in **Vue**, and a **6-week** deadline. Search engines must index the public help pages, but the logged-in area does not need indexing.
tldr: Two Vue developers, 6 weeks, public help pages need SEO.

qs.q: Which full-stack web framework should the portal use?
qs.about: Both frameworks add server rendering, routing and an API layer on top of a UI library.
qs.why: The framework fixes the language of your components for the whole project, so it sets how fast the team can move.

opts.d: The Vue framework. Your team already writes Vue components.

i: No new library to learn for the team
Auto-imports and file conventions reduce boilerplate
Smaller ecosystem of ready-made portal components

opts.d: The React framework. Requires writing components in React.

i: Larger ecosystem and more hiring options
The team must learn React: **plan 2 to 3 weeks** of slower work
A 6-week deadline leaves little room for that

qs.about: Public help pages need HTML ready for search engines. The logged-in area does not.
qs.why: The rendering style decides your hosting cost and how fast pages feel.

vis.cap: Where the HTML is produced in each style.
t: /help/*  ──built once──▶  static files on a CDN     (indexed by search engines)
/app/*   ──in browser──▶  single-page app           (not indexed, not needed)
any page ──every visit─▶  server builds the HTML    (needs an always-on server)

opts.t: Hybrid: static help pages, client-side app
opts.d: Help pages are built once. The logged-in area runs in the browser.
The server builds each page on each visit.

qs.about: You can pick more than one if you want a fallback or a staging environment.

opts.t: A static host plus a small API
opts.d: Static files on a CDN; the API on a managed service.
One container runs the whole app.

i: Nobody on the team can operate containers
